title.en: military governor of the Weiwu Army

units.zh: 王審知，字信通，光州固始人也。
units.en: Wang Shenzhi, whose style name was Xintong, came from Gushi in Guang Prefecture.
units.literal: Wang Shenzhi, styled Xintong, was a native of Gushi in Guang Prefecture.

units.zh: 父恁，世為農。
units.en: His father Ren's family had farmed for generations.
units.literal: His father Ren's family had been farmers for generations.

units.zh: 兄潮，為縣史。
units.en: His elder brother Chao held the post of county clerk.
units.literal: His elder brother Chao served as a county clerk.

units.zh: 唐末群盜起，壽州人王緒攻陷固始，緒聞潮兄弟材勇，召置軍中，以潮為軍校。
units.en: When the Tang dynasty was collapsing and rebels swarmed the realm, a man from Shou Prefecture named Wang Xu seized Gushi. Hearing of the Chao brothers' courage and ability, Xu enrolled them in his forces and appointed Chao a company commander.
units.literal: At the end of the Tang, bandits rose everywhere; Wang Xu of Shou Prefecture captured Gushi; Xu heard that the Chao brothers were talented and brave, summoned them into his army, and made Chao a military officer.

units.zh: 是時，蔡州秦宗權方募士以益兵，乃以緒為光州刺史，召其兵會擊黃巢。
units.en: Qin Zongquan of Cai Prefecture was then recruiting soldiers to swell his ranks. He named Xu governor of Guang Prefecture and called on his troops to march with him against Huang Chao.
units.literal: At that time Qin Zongquan of Cai Prefecture was recruiting men to augment his troops; he therefore appointed Xu governor of Guang Prefecture and summoned his army to join in attacking Huang Chao.

units.zh: 緒遲留不行，宗權發兵攻緒。
units.en: Xu lingered and refused to move, so Zongquan sent an army against him.
units.literal: Xu delayed and would not advance; Zongquan sent troops to attack him.

units.zh: 緒率眾南奔，所至剽掠，自南康入臨汀，陷漳浦，有眾數萬。
units.en: Xu fled south with his host, looting every district they passed through. They marched from Nankang into Linting, took Zhangpu, and mustered a force of tens of thousands.
units.literal: Xu led his multitude south in flight, plundering wherever they went; from Nankang they entered Linting, captured Zhangpu, and had a force of several tens of thousands.

units.zh: 緒性猜忌，部將有材能者，多因事殺之，潮頗自懼。
units.en: Xu was suspicious by temperament and routinely found excuses to kill capable subordinates. Chao began to fear for his life.
units.literal: Xu was by nature suspicious; subordinate officers who had ability he often killed on one pretext or another, and Chao grew quite fearful for himself.

units.zh: 軍次南安，潮說其前鋒將曰：「吾屬棄墳墓、妻子而為盜者，為緒所脅爾，豈其本心哉！
units.en: When the army encamped at Nan'an, Chao addressed the vanguard commander: "We left our ancestors' graves and our families behind to live as outlaws only because Xu forced us—surely that was never what we wanted!
units.literal: When the army halted at Nan'an, Chao said to the vanguard commander: "We abandoned graves, wives, and children to become bandits only because Xu coerced us—was that truly our hearts' desire!

units.zh: 今緒雄猜，將吏之材能者必死，吾屬不自保朝夕，況欲圖成事哉！」
units.en: Xu is brutal and mistrustful now; any officer with talent is as good as dead. We cannot count on living from one day to the next, much less hope to achieve anything lasting!"
units.literal: Now Xu is fierce and suspicious; officers and clerks with ability are certain to die—we cannot preserve ourselves from morning to night, let alone plan to accomplish great deeds!"

units.zh: 前鋒將大悟，與潮相持而泣。
units.en: The vanguard commander was deeply moved; he and Chao clung to each other and wept.
units.literal: The vanguard commander was greatly enlightened and, embracing Chao, wept with him.

units.zh: 乃選壯士數十人，伏篁竹間，伺緒至，躍出擒之，囚之軍中，緒所自殺。
units.en: They chose several dozen strong men, concealed them in a bamboo thicket, and when Xu arrived sprang out to seize him and hold him prisoner in the camp. Xu then killed himself.
units.literal: They then selected several dozen stalwart men, hid among bamboo groves, waited until Xu arrived, leaped out and seized him, and imprisoned him in the camp; Xu killed himself.

units.zh: 緒已見廢，前鋒將曰：「生我者潮也。」
units.en: With Xu deposed, the vanguard commander declared, "Chao gave me life."
units.literal: Xu having been deposed, the vanguard commander said: "Chao gave me life."

units.zh: 乃推潮為主。
units.en: They then made Chao their leader.
units.literal: They then installed Chao as their leader.

units.zh: 是時，泉州刺史廖彥若為政貪暴，泉人苦之，聞潮略地至其境，而軍行整肅，其耆老相率遮道留之，潮即引兵圍彥若，逾年克之。
units.en: Quanzhou prefect Liao Yanruo ruled with greed and cruelty, and the people hated him. When they heard that Chao's army had reached their borders and marched with discipline, elders blocked the road and begged him to stay. Chao besieged Yanruo and captured the city after more than a year.
units.literal: At that time Quanzhou prefect Liao Yanruo governed with greed and cruelty, and the people of Quan suffered. Hearing that Chao's forces had reached their borders and marched in good order, elders met him on the road and begged him to stay. Chao then besieged Yanruo and took the city after more than a year.

units.zh: 光啟二年，福建觀察使陳巖表潮泉州刺史。
units.en: In the second year of the Guangqi era, Fujian observation commissioner Chen Yan recommended Chao for Quanzhou prefect.
units.literal: In the second year of Guangqi, Fujian observation commissioner Chen Yan memorialized Chao as Quanzhou prefect.

units.zh: 景福元年巖卒，其壻范暉自稱留後。
units.en: In the first year of Jingfu, Chen Yan died and his son-in-law Fan Hui declared himself acting governor.
units.literal: In the first year of Jingfu, Chen Yan died and his son-in-law Fan Hui styled himself acting governor.

units.zh: 潮遣審知攻暉，久不克，士卒傷死甚眾，審知請班師，潮不許。
units.en: Chao sent Shenzhi to besiege Hui, but the city held out for a long time and casualties mounted. Shenzhi asked to withdraw; Chao refused.
units.literal: Chao sent Shenzhi to attack Hui, but after a long siege could not capture the city; many soldiers were wounded and killed. Shenzhi asked to withdraw, but Chao refused.

units.zh: 又請潮自臨軍，且益兵，潮報曰：「兵與將俱盡，吾當自往。」
units.en: Shenzhi then asked Chao to take command in person and send more troops. Chao answered, "When soldiers and generals are all exhausted, I shall come myself."
units.literal: Shenzhi then asked Chao to come supervise the army in person and send reinforcements. Chao replied: "When soldiers and commanders are all spent, I shall go myself."

units.zh: 審知乃親督士卒攻破之，暉見殺。
units.en: Shenzhi personally led the assault and broke through; Hui was killed.
units.literal: Shenzhi personally directed the assault and broke through; Hui was killed.

units.zh: 唐即以潮為福建觀察使，潮以審知為副使。
units.en: The Tang court promptly appointed Chao Fujian observation commissioner and made Shenzhi his deputy.
units.literal: The Tang court immediately appointed Chao Fujian observation commissioner and made Shenzhi his deputy.

units.zh: 審知為人狀皃雄偉，隆準方口，常乘白馬，軍中號「白馬三郎」。
units.en: Shenzhi was a man of imposing build, with a prominent nose and square jaw. He habitually rode a white horse, and the troops nicknamed him "Third Son on the White Horse."
units.literal: Shenzhi in person was imposing in stature, with a high nose and square mouth; he often rode a white horse, and in the army they called him "Third Son on the White Horse."

units.zh: 乾寧四年，潮卒，審知代立。
units.en: In the fourth year of the Qianning era, Chao died and Shenzhi took his place as leader.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Qianning, Chao died and Shenzhi succeeded him in power.

units.zh: 唐以福州為威武軍，拜審知節度使，累遷同中書門下平章事，封瑯琊王。
units.en: The Tang court organized Fuzhou as the Weiwu military circuit and appointed Shenzhi its governor. He rose through successive promotions to Grand Councilor and was enfeoffed as Prince of Langya.
units.literal: The Tang made Fuzhou the Weiwu Army district, appointed Shenzhi military governor, repeatedly promoted him to Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Langya.

units.zh: 唐亡，梁太祖加拜審知中書令，封閩王，升福州為大都督府。
units.en: After the Tang fell, the Liang founding emperor invested Shenzhi as Director of the Secretariat and King of Min, and raised Fuzhou to the status of a metropolitan prefecture.
units.literal: When the Tang perished, the Liang founding emperor further appointed Shenzhi Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed him as King of Min, and elevated Fuzhou to a great metropolitan prefecture.

units.zh: 是時，楊行密據有江淮，審知歲遣使泛海，自登、萊朝貢於梁，使者入海，覆溺常十三四。
units.en: Yang Xingmi then controlled the lower Yangtze, so Shenzhi sent annual missions by sea from Deng and Lai to pay tribute to the Liang. Roughly three or four envoys in ten were lost when their ships foundered at sea.
units.literal: At that time Yang Xingmi held the Jianghuai region; Shenzhi each year sent envoys by sea from Deng and Lai to present tribute to the Liang; when the envoys entered the ocean, shipwrecks commonly claimed three or four out of ten.

units.zh: 審知雖起盜賊，而為人儉約，好禮下士。
units.en: Though Shenzhi had begun as a rebel, in office he lived simply, honored ritual, and treated men of learning with respect.
units.literal: Although Shenzhi had risen from banditry, as a man he was frugal and restrained, honored ritual, and treated scholars with deference.

units.zh: 王淡，唐相溥之子；
units.en: Wang Dan, son of the Tang chancellor Wang Pu;
units.literal: Wang Dan, son of the Tang chancellor Wang Pu;

units.zh: 楊沂，唐相涉從弟；
units.en: Yang Yi, a cousin of the Tang chancellor Yang She;
units.literal: Yang Yi, a younger cousin of the Tang chancellor Yang She;

units.zh: 徐寅，唐時知名進士，皆依審知仕宦。
units.en: and Xu Yin, a celebrated Tang jinshi—all took service under Shenzhi.
units.literal: and Xu Yin, a renowned jinshi degree-holder of the Tang—all relied on Shenzhi and entered official service under him.

units.zh: 又建學四門，以教閩士之秀者。
units.en: He also established a Four Gates Academy to educate the most promising scholars of Min.
units.literal: He also founded a Four Gates Academy to instruct the finest scholars of Min.

units.zh: 招來海中蠻夷商賈。
units.en: He drew overseas merchants from the southern seas to trade in his ports.
units.literal: He attracted barbarian merchants from across the sea.

units.zh: 海上黃崎，波濤為陰，一夕風雨雷電震擊，開以為港，閩人以為審知德政所致，號為甘棠港。
units.en: At Huangqi on the coast, treacherous seas had long blocked the approach. One night a storm of wind, rain, thunder, and lightning tore open a channel that became a harbor. The people of Min credited Shenzhi's benevolent rule and called it Sweet Pear Harbor.
units.literal: At Huangqi on the sea, waves and billows had blocked the passage; in one night wind, rain, thunder, and lightning struck and opened it as a harbor; the people of Min believed this was due to Shenzhi's virtuous government and named it Sweet Pear Harbor.

units.zh: 審知同光三年卒，年六十四，謚曰忠懿。
units.en: Shenzhi died in the third year of Tongguang at the age of sixty-four. He was given the posthumous title Loyal and Cultivated.
units.literal: Shenzhi died in the third year of Tongguang, aged sixty-four; his posthumous title was Loyal and Cultivated.

units.zh: 子延翰立。
units.en: His son Yanhan took the throne.
units.literal: His son Yanhan succeeded him.

units.zh: 延翰字子逸，審知長子也。
units.en: Yanhan, whose style name was Ziyi, was Shenzhi's eldest son.
units.literal: Yanhan, styled Ziyi, was Shenzhi's eldest son.

units.zh: 同光四年，唐拜延翰節度使。
units.en: In the fourth year of Tongguang the Tang court appointed Yanhan military governor of the circuit.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Tongguang the Tang appointed Yanhan military governor.

units.zh: 是歲，莊宗遇弒，中國多故，延翰乃取司馬遷《史記》閩越王無諸傳示其將吏曰：「閩，自古王國也，吾今不王，何待之有？」
units.en: That year Emperor Zhuangzong was murdered and the empire fell into disorder. Yanhan produced from Sima Qian's Records the biography of Wuzhu, king of ancient Minyue, and showed it to his commanders and officials, saying, "Min has been a kingdom since antiquity. If I do not claim kingship now, how long should I wait?"
units.literal: That year Emperor Zhuangzong was assassinated and the central realm was in turmoil; Yanhan then took Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian, the biography of Minyue's King Wuzhu, and showed it to his generals and officials, saying: "Min has been a kingdom since antiquity—if I do not become king now, what am I waiting for?"

units.zh: 於是軍府將吏上書勸進。
units.en: His generals and staff then submitted a joint memorial urging him to take the throne.
units.literal: Thereupon the generals and officials of the military administration submitted a memorial urging him to ascend.

units.zh: 十月，延翰建國稱王，而猶稟唐正朔。
units.en: In the tenth month Yanhan founded his kingdom and proclaimed himself king, while still observing the Tang reign era in official documents.
units.literal: In the tenth month Yanhan established his state and declared himself king, yet still acknowledged the Tang calendar.

units.zh: 延翰為人長大，美皙如玉，其妻崔氏陋而淫，延翰不能制。
units.en: Yanhan was tall and handsome, with skin fair as jade. His wife Lady Cui was homely and unchaste, and he could not restrain her.
units.literal: Yanhan was tall in stature, fair and lustrous as jade; his wife the Lady Cui was plain and licentious, and Yanhan could not control her.

units.zh: 審知喪未期，徹其几筵，又多選良家子為妾。
units.en: Before his father's mourning year was out he cleared away the mourning furnishings and took numerous daughters of respectable families as concubines.
units.literal: Before Shenzhi's mourning period had ended, he removed the mourning tables and also selected many daughters of good families as concubines.

units.zh: 崔氏性妒，良家子之美者，輒幽之別室，系以大械，刻木為人手以擊頰，又以鐵錐刺之，一歲中死者八十四人。
units.en: Lady Cui was fiercely jealous. Whenever a concubine from a respectable family was beautiful, Cui locked her in a side room, bound her in heavy irons, had a wooden hand carved to slap her face, and stabbed her with iron spikes. Within a single year eighty-four women died at her hands.
units.literal: The Lady Cui was jealous by nature; whenever a daughter of a good family was beautiful she would confine her in a separate chamber, bind her with heavy fetters, carve a wooden hand to strike her cheeks, and also stab her with iron awls—in one year eighty-four died.

units.zh: 崔氏後病，見以為祟而卒。
units.en: Lady Cui later fell ill, believed she was haunted by their spirits, and died.
units.literal: The Lady Cui later fell ill, saw them as malign spirits, and died.

units.zh: 審知養子建州刺史延稟，本姓周氏，自審知時與延翰不葉。
units.en: Shenzhi's adopted son Yanbin, governor of Jianzhou, had been born a Zhou. He and Yanhan had been at odds since Shenzhi's day.
units.literal: Shenzhi's adopted son Yanbin, prefect of Jian Prefecture, was originally surnamed Zhou; since Shenzhi's time he and Yanhan had not been on good terms.

units.zh: 延翰立，以其弟延鈞為泉州刺史，延鈞怒。
units.en: After Yanhan came to power he appointed his younger brother Yanjun prefect of Quanzhou, a slight that enraged Yanjun.
units.literal: When Yanhan took power he made his younger brother Yanjun prefect of Quanzhou; Yanjun was angry.

units.zh: 二人因謀作亂。
units.en: The two of them then conspired to rebel.
units.literal: The two men therefore plotted rebellion.

units.zh: 十二月，延稟、延鈞皆以兵入，執延翰殺之。
units.en: In the twelfth month Yanbin and Yanjun marched in with their armies, seized Yanhan, and put him to death.
units.literal: In the twelfth month Yanbin and Yanjun both entered with troops, seized Yanhan, and killed him.

units.zh: 而延鈞立，更名鏻。
units.en: Yanjun then assumed rule and changed his personal name to Lin.
units.literal: Yanjun then took power and changed his name to Lin.

units.zh: 鏻，審知次子也。
units.en: Lin was Shenzhi's second son.
units.literal: Lin was Shenzhi's second son.

units.zh: 唐即拜鏻節度使，累加檢校太師、中書令，封閩王。
units.en: The Tang court promptly appointed Lin military governor and successively honored him with the honorary titles Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffing him as King of Min.
units.literal: The Tang immediately appointed Lin military governor, repeatedly added the titles of Honorary Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed him as King of Min.

units.zh: 初，延稟與鏻之謀殺延翰也，延稟之兵先至，已執延翰而殺之，膽日鏻兵始至，延稟自以養子，推鏻而立之。
units.en: When Yanbin and Lin had plotted to kill Yanhan, Yanbin's forces arrived first and had already seized and executed him. Lin's troops came only the following day. As an adopted son, Yanbin deferred and set Lin on the throne.
units.literal: Earlier, when Yanbin and Lin plotted to kill Yanhan, Yanbin's troops arrived first, had already seized Yanhan and killed him; the next day Lin's troops arrived; Yanbin, considering himself an adopted son, yielded and installed Lin.

units.zh: 延稟還建州，鏻餞於郊，延稟臨訣謂鏻曰：「善繼先誌，毋煩老兄復來！」
units.en: Yanbin returned to Jianzhou, and Lin escorted him to the outskirts of the city. At their farewell Yanbin told him, "Uphold our forefathers' legacy—and do not make your elder brother march here again!"
units.literal: Yanbin returned to Jian Prefecture; Lin saw him off in the suburbs; at parting Yanbin said to Lin: "Carry on our forefathers' aims well—do not trouble your elder brother to come again!"

units.zh: 鏻銜之。
units.en: Lin nursed a grudge over the remark.
units.literal: Lin harbored resentment over this.

units.zh: 長興二年，延稟率兵擊鏻，攻其西門，使其子繼雄轉海攻其南門，鏻遣王仁達拒之。
units.en: In the second year of Changxing, Yanbin marched against Lin, assaulting the western gate while his son Jixiong sailed around to attack the southern gate. Lin sent Wang Renda to meet them.
units.literal: In the second year of Changxing, Yanbin led troops to attack Lin, assaulting his western gate and sending his son Jixiong by sea to strike the southern gate; Lin dispatched Wang Renda to resist.

units.zh: 仁達伏甲舟中，偽立白幟請降，繼雄信之，登舟，伏兵發，刺殺之，梟其首西門，其兵見之皆潰去，延稟見執。
units.en: Renda concealed armored men aboard his vessels and hoisted white flags in a feigned surrender. Jixiong believed him, came aboard, and the hidden soldiers leaped out and killed him. Renda displayed Jixiong's head at the western gate; at the sight his army broke and fled. Yanbin was taken prisoner.
units.literal: Renda hid armored men in the boats, falsely raised white banners to request surrender; Jixiong believed him, boarded the boat, the ambush sprang forth and stabbed him to death; his head was displayed at the western gate; his troops, seeing it, all fled; Yanbin was captured.

units.zh: 鏻誚之曰：「予不能繼先誌，果煩老兄復來！」
units.en: Lin taunted him: "So I failed to uphold our forefathers' legacy, and your elder brother really did have to come again!"
units.literal: Lin mocked him, saying: "I could not carry on our forefathers' aims—so it truly did trouble my elder brother to come again!"

units.zh: 延廩不能對，遂殺之。
units.en: Yanbin had no answer and was executed on the spot.
units.literal: Yanbin could not reply and was then killed.

units.zh: 延稟子繼升守建州，聞敗，奔於錢塘。
units.en: Yanbin's son Jisheng was defending Jianzhou. When he heard of the defeat he fled to Qiantang.
units.literal: Yanbin's son Jisheng held Jian Prefecture; hearing of the defeat, he fled to Qiantang.

units.zh: 長興三年，鏻上書言：「楚王馬殷、吳越王錢鏐皆為尚書令，今皆已薨，請授臣尚書令。」
units.en: In the third year of Changxing, Lin memorialized: "King Ma Yin of Chu and King Qian Liu of Wuyue were both Directors of the Secretariat; both are now dead—please grant me that office."
units.literal: In the third year of Changxing, Lin memorialized: "King Ma Yin of Chu and King Qian Liu of Wuyue were both Directors of the Secretariat; both are now deceased—please grant me that office."

units.zh: 唐不報，鏻遂絕朝貢。
units.en: The Tang court did not reply, and Lin cut off tribute.
units.literal: The Tang court gave no response, and Lin thereupon cut off tribute.

units.zh: 鏻好鬼神、道家之說，道士陳守元以左道見信，建寶皇宮以居之。
units.en: Lin was devoted to spirits and Daoist lore. The Daoist Chen Shouyuan won his confidence through occult practices, and Lin built the Precious Imperial Palace for him to live in.
units.literal: Lin favored spirits and ghosts and Daoist teachings; the Daoist Chen Shouyuan, through heterodox arts, won his trust, and he built the Precious Imperial Palace for him to dwell in.

units.zh: 守元謂鏻曰：「寶皇命王少避其位，後當為六十年天子。」
units.en: Shouyuan told Lin, "The Precious Emperor orders you to step aside for a time. Afterward you will reign as Son of Heaven for sixty years."
units.literal: Shouyuan said to Lin: "The Precious Emperor commands the king briefly to yield his seat; afterward he shall be Son of Heaven for sixty years."

units.zh: 鏻欣然遜位，命其子繼鵬權主府事。
units.en: Delighted, Lin abdicated and put his son Jipeng in charge of government affairs.
units.literal: Lin gladly abdicated and ordered his son Jipeng to administer the prefectural affairs provisionally.

units.zh: 既而復位，遣守元問寶皇：「六十年後將安歸？」
units.en: He soon took the throne back and sent Shouyuan to inquire of the Precious Emperor, "Where shall I go when the sixty years are done?"
units.literal: He then resumed the throne and sent Shouyuan to ask the Precious Emperor: "After sixty years, whither shall I go?"

units.zh: 守元傳寶皇語曰：「六十年後，當為大羅仙人。」
units.en: Shouyuan brought back the answer: "After sixty years you will become an immortal of the Great Canopy Heaven."
units.literal: Shouyuan relayed the Precious Emperor's words: "After sixty years you shall become a Great Canopy Immortal."

units.zh: 鏻乃即皇帝位，受冊於寶皇，以黃龍見真封宅，改元為龍啟，國號閩。
units.en: Lin thereupon declared himself emperor, received his mandate from the Precious Emperor, took up residence in the Yellow Dragon Manifest Truth palace, adopted the era name Dragon Inception, and proclaimed the state of Min.
units.literal: Lin then assumed the imperial throne, received investiture from the Precious Emperor, took the Yellow Dragon Manifest Truth Sealed Residence as his dwelling, changed the era name to Dragon Inception, and made the state name Min.

units.zh: 追謚審知為昭武孝皇帝，廟號太祖，立五廟，置百官，以福州為長樂府。
units.en: He posthumously honored Shenzhi as Emperor Zhaowu the Filial, with the temple name Taizu, established five ancestral temples, appointed a full court, and renamed Fuzhou the Changle metropolitan prefecture.
units.literal: He posthumously titled Shenzhi Emperor Zhaowu Xiaohuang, temple name Taizu, established five ancestral temples, installed the full bureaucracy, and made Fuzhou the Changle Metropolitan Prefecture.

units.zh: 而閩地狹，國用不足，以中軍使薛文傑為國計使。
units.en: Min's territory was small and revenues scarce, so he appointed the Central Army Commissioner Xue Wenjie national revenue commissioner.
units.literal: But Min's territory was narrow and state revenue insufficient; he made the Central Army Commissioner Xue Wenjie national revenue commissioner.

units.zh: 文傑多察民間陰事，致富人以罪，而籍沒其貲以佐用，閩人皆怨。
units.en: Wenjie pried into private affairs throughout the realm, framed wealthy families on trumped-up charges, and confiscated their goods to fill the treasury. The people of Min hated him.
units.literal: Wenjie often investigated private matters among the people, charged the wealthy with crimes, and confiscated their property to supplement expenditures; all the people of Min resented him.

units.zh: 又薦妖巫徐彥，曰：「陛下左右多奸臣，不質諸鬼神，將為亂。」
units.en: He also recommended the sorcerer Xu Yan, saying, "Your Majesty is surrounded by traitors. Unless you test them through spirits, rebellion will follow."
units.literal: He also recommended the sorcerer Xu Yan, saying: "Around Your Majesty are many treacherous ministers; if you do not verify them through spirits and ghosts, there will be rebellion."

units.zh: 鏻使彥視鬼於宮中。
units.en: Lin ordered Yan to divine for ghosts within the palace.
units.literal: Lin had Yan observe ghosts within the palace.

units.zh: 文傑與內樞密使吳英有隙，英病在告，文傑謂英曰：「上以公居近密，而屢以疾告，將罷公。」
units.en: Wenjie bore a grudge against the Inner Palace Military Affairs Commissioner Wu Ying. While Ying was on sick leave Wenjie told him, "The emperor thinks that because you hold a post at court you ought not keep pleading illness. He means to remove you."
units.literal: Wenjie had a rift with the Inner Palace Military Affairs Commissioner Wu Ying; Ying was ill on leave; Wenjie said to Ying: "The emperor, seeing that you hold a post close to the inner quarters yet repeatedly report illness, will dismiss you."

units.zh: 英曰：「奈何？」
units.en: Ying asked, "What can I do?"
units.literal: Ying said: "What is to be done?"

units.zh: 文傑因教英曰：「即上遣人問公疾，當言『頭痛而已，無他苦也。』」
units.en: Wenjie coached him: "When the emperor sends someone to ask after your health, say only, 'A headache—nothing more serious than that.'"
units.literal: Wenjie then instructed Ying: "When the emperor next sends someone to inquire about your illness, you should say, 'Only a headache—no other affliction.'"

units.zh: 英以為然。
units.en: Ying agreed that this was wise counsel.
units.literal: Ying thought this sound.

units.zh: 明日，諷鏻使巫視英疾，巫言：「入北廟，見英為崇順王所訊，曰：『汝何敢謀反？』
units.en: The next day he persuaded Lin to have the sorcerer divine Ying's illness. The sorcerer reported, "In the northern temple I saw Ying questioned by King Chongshun, who demanded, 'How dare you plot rebellion?'
units.literal: The next day he prompted Lin to have the sorcerer examine Ying's illness; the sorcerer said: "Entering the northern temple, I saw Ying interrogated by King Chongshun, who said: 'How dare you plot rebellion?'

units.zh: 以金槌擊其首。」
units.en: He struck his head with a golden mallet."
units.literal: He struck his head with a golden mallet."

units.zh: 鏻以語文傑，文傑曰：「未可信也，宜問其疾如何。」
units.en: Lin told Wenjie what the sorcerer had said. Wenjie replied, "That alone proves nothing. Ask what his illness actually is."
units.literal: Lin reported this to Wenjie; Wenjie said: "This cannot yet be trusted; you should ask what his illness is like."

units.zh: 鏻遣人問之，英曰：「頭痛。」
units.en: Lin sent an envoy to Ying, who answered, "A headache."
units.literal: Lin sent someone to inquire; Ying said: "A headache."

units.zh: 鏻以為然，即以英下獄，命文傑劾之，英自誣伏，見殺。
units.en: Lin took this as confirmation, threw Ying into prison, and ordered Wenjie to prosecute him. Ying confessed to the fabricated charge and was executed.
units.literal: Lin believed it; he immediately imprisoned Ying, ordered Wenjie to prosecute him; Ying confessed to the false charge and was killed.

units.zh: 英嘗主閩兵，得其軍士心，軍士聞英死，皆怒。
units.en: Ying had once commanded the Min armies and won the soldiers' loyalty. When the troops learned of his death they were furious.
units.literal: Ying had once commanded Min's troops and won the soldiers' hearts; when the soldiers heard Ying was dead, all were enraged.

units.zh: 是歲，吳人攻建州，鏻遣其將王延宗救之，兵士在道不肯進，曰：「得文傑乃進。」
units.en: That year the Wu attacked Jianzhou. Lin sent his general Wang Yancong to relieve the city, but the troops on the march refused to go forward, crying, "Hand over Wenjie, then we march!"
units.literal: That year the Wu people attacked Jian Prefecture; Lin sent his general Wang Yancong to rescue it; the soldiers on the march refused to advance, saying: "We advance only when we get Wenjie."

units.zh: 鏻惜之不與，其子繼鵬請與之以紓難，乃以檻車送文傑軍中。
units.en: Lin was loath to surrender him. His son Jipeng urged that Wenjie be given up to avert disaster, and Wenjie was sent to the army in a prison cart.
units.literal: Lin was reluctant and would not give him up; his son Jipeng asked to surrender him to ease the crisis; they then sent Wenjie in a caged cart to the army.

units.zh: 文傑善數術，自占云：「過三日可無患。」
units.en: Wenjie was skilled in divination and cast his own fortune, saying, "In three days I shall be safe."
units.literal: Wenjie was skilled in numerology; he divined for himself and said: "After three days I shall be free of trouble."

units.zh: 送者聞之，疾馳二日而至，軍士踴躍，磔文傑於市，閩人爭以瓦石投之，臠食立盡。
units.en: Hearing this, the escorts spurred their horses and reached the army in two days instead of three. The soldiers erupted in joy, dismembered Wenjie in the marketplace, and the people of Min pelted his body with tiles and stones until every scrap of flesh was gone.
units.literal: The escorts heard this and galloped hard, arriving in two days; the soldiers leaped for joy, dismembered Wenjie in the marketplace, and the people of Min vied to pelt him with tiles and stones until his flesh was devoured on the spot.

units.zh: 明日，鏻使者至，赦之，已不及。
units.en: The next day Lin's messenger arrived with an order of pardon, but it was too late.
units.literal: The next day Lin's envoy arrived with a pardon—it was already too late.

units.zh: 初，文傑為鏻造檻車，以謂古制疏闊，乃更其制，令上下通，中以鐵芒內向，動輒觸之，既成，首被其毒。
units.en: Wenjie had once designed a prison cart for Lin, finding the old model too loose. He redesigned it with open top and bottom and inward-pointing iron spikes so that any movement drew blood. When it was finished he became its first victim.
units.literal: Earlier Wenjie had built a caged cart for Lin, considering the ancient design too loose; he therefore redesigned it so that top and bottom communicated, with iron spikes pointing inward in the middle—at the slightest movement one was pricked—and when it was finished he was the first to suffer from it.

units.zh: 龍啟三年，改元永和。
units.en: In the third year of Dragon Inception he adopted the era name Eternal Harmony.
units.literal: In the third year of Dragon Inception he changed the era name to Eternal Harmony.

units.zh: 王仁達為鏻殺延稟有功，而典親兵，鏻心忌之，嘗問仁達曰：「趙高指鹿為馬，以愚二世，果有之邪？」
units.en: Wang Renda had distinguished himself by killing Yanbin and now commanded the imperial guard. Lin grew jealous and once asked him, "Did Zhao Gao really point to a deer and call it a horse to deceive the Second Emperor?"
units.literal: Wang Renda had merit for killing Yanbin on Lin's behalf and commanded the personal guard; Lin harbored suspicion in his heart and once asked Renda: "When Zhao Gao called a deer a horse to deceive the Second Emperor—did that truly happen?"

units.zh: 仁達曰：「秦二世愚，故高指鹿為馬，非高能愚二世也。
units.en: Renda replied, "The Second Emperor of Qin was a fool, which is why Gao could call a deer a horse. Gao did not make the emperor foolish—the emperor was already foolish.
units.literal: Renda said: "The Second Emperor of Qin was foolish, so Gao called a deer a horse—it was not that Gao could make the Second Emperor foolish.

units.zh: 今陛下聰明，朝廷官不滿百，起居動靜，陛下皆知之，敢有作威福者，族滅之而已。」
units.en: Your Majesty is intelligent, the court has fewer than a hundred officials, and you know every movement at court. Anyone who dared abuse his power could simply be exterminated along with his clan."
units.literal: Today Your Majesty is wise; the court officials number fewer than a hundred; your comings and goings and every movement Your Majesty knows—who would dare wield power for private ends? Exterminate his clan, that is all."

units.zh: 鏻慚，賜與金帛慰安之。
units.en: Lin was abashed and rewarded him with gold and silk to reassure him.
units.literal: Lin was ashamed and bestowed gold and silk to comfort him.

units.zh: 退而謂人曰：「仁達智略，在吾世可用，不可遺後世患。」
units.en: Afterward he told his attendants, "Renda's talent is useful while I live, but he must not be left as a threat to my heirs."
units.literal: Afterward he said to others: "Renda's wisdom and stratagems can be used in my lifetime; he must not be left as a trouble for later generations."

units.zh: 卒誣以罪殺之。
units.en: In the end he fabricated charges and had him executed.
units.literal: In the end he framed him on a charge and killed him.

units.zh: 鏻妻早卒，繼室金氏賢而不見答。
units.en: Lin's first wife died young. His second wife, Lady Jin, was virtuous but went unloved.
units.literal: Lin's wife died early; his second wife the Lady Jin was worthy yet received no favor.

units.zh: 審知婢金鳳，姓陳氏，鏻嬖之，遂立以為後。
units.en: Golden Phoenix, a maid of Shenzhi's from the Chen clan, became Lin's favorite and was raised to empress.
units.literal: Shenzhi's maid Golden Phoenix, surnamed Chen, Lin favored and then installed as empress.

units.zh: 初，鏻有嬖吏歸守明者，以色見倖，號歸郎，鏻後得風疾，陳氏與歸郎奸。
units.en: Lin once kept a favorite clerk named Gui Shouming, who won his affection by his beauty and was nicknamed Lord Gui. After Lin fell ill with paralysis, Empress Chen and Lord Gui became lovers.
units.literal: Earlier Lin had a favored clerk Gui Shouming who won favor through his looks and was called Lord Gui; Lin later contracted wind illness, and the Lady Chen and Lord Gui committed adultery.

units.zh: 又有百工院使李可殷，因歸郎以通陳氏。
units.en: Li Keyin, commissioner of the Hundred Crafts Bureau, also gained access to the empress through Lord Gui.
units.literal: There was also the Hundred Crafts Bureau Commissioner Li Keyin, who through Lord Gui gained access to the Lady Chen.

units.zh: 鏻命錦工作九龍帳，國人歌曰：「誰謂九龍帳，惟貯一歸郎！」
units.en: Lin ordered the brocade workshops to weave a Nine Dragons canopy. The people sang, "They call it the Nine Dragons canopy, but it holds only Lord Gui!"
units.literal: Lin ordered the brocade workers to make a Nine Dragons canopy; the people sang: "Who says the Nine Dragons canopy holds anything but one Lord Gui!"

units.zh: 鏻婢春燕有色，其子繼鵬蒸之，鏻已病，繼鵬因陳氏以求春燕，鏻怏怏與之。
units.en: Spring Swallow, a maid in Lin's household, was beautiful. His son Jipeng took her as a concubine. Already gravely ill, Lin yielded her to Jipeng at Empress Chen's urging, though he did so with bitter reluctance.
units.literal: Lin's maid Spring Swallow was beautiful; his son Jipeng took her as a concubine; Lin was already ill; Jipeng through the Lady Chen asked for Spring Swallow; Lin reluctantly gave her to him.

units.zh: 其次子繼韜怒，謀殺繼鵬，繼鵬懼，與皇城使李仿圖之。
units.en: His second son Jitao, enraged, plotted to kill Jipeng. Jipeng, in fear, conspired with the Imperial City Commissioner Li Fang.
units.literal: His second son Jitao was angry and plotted to kill Jipeng; Jipeng was afraid and, with the Imperial City Commissioner Li Fang, plotted against him.

units.zh: 是歲十月，鏻饗軍於大酺殿，坐中昏然，言見延稟來，仿以為鏻病已甚，乃令壯士先殺李可殷於家。
units.en: In the tenth month of that year Lin feasted his troops in the Great Revelry Hall. Midway through the banquet he fell into a stupor and cried that Yanbin had come for him. Fang judged Lin's illness beyond recovery and sent bravos to kill Li Keyin at his home.
units.literal: That year in the tenth month Lin feasted the army in the Great Revelry Hall; mid-feast he grew dazed and said he saw Yanbin coming; Fang thought Lin's illness was already grave and ordered stalwart men first to kill Li Keyin at his home.

units.zh: 明日晨朝，鏻無恙，問仿殺可殷何罪，仿懼而出，與繼鵬率皇城衛士而入。
units.en: The next morning Lin appeared at court unharmed and demanded to know what crime had justified Keyin's murder. Fang fled in terror and, with Jipeng, led the Imperial City guards into the palace.
units.literal: The next morning at court audience Lin was unharmed and asked Fang what crime Keyin had committed to be killed; Fang fled in fear and, with Jipeng, led the Imperial City guards inside.

units.zh: 鏻聞鼓噪聲，走匿九龍帳中，衛士刺之不殂，宮人不忍其苦，為絕之。
units.en: Hearing the uproar, Lin fled into the Nine Dragons canopy. The guards stabbed him but failed to kill him outright, and the palace women, unable to bear his agony, finished him off.
units.literal: Hearing the clamor of drums, Lin ran and hid in the Nine Dragons canopy; the guards stabbed him but did not kill him; palace women could not bear his suffering and finished him off.

units.zh: 繼韜及陳後、歸郎皆為仿所殺。
units.en: Jitao, Empress Chen, and Lord Gui were all killed by Fang.
units.literal: Jitao, Empress Chen, and Lord Gui were all killed by Fang.

units.zh: 鏻立十年見殺，謚曰惠皇帝，廟號太宗。
units.en: Lin had ruled ten years when he was murdered. He was posthumously titled Emperor Hui, with the temple name Taizong.
units.literal: Lin had reigned ten years when he was killed; his posthumous title was Emperor Hui, temple name Taizong.

units.zh: 繼鵬，鏻長子也。
units.en: Jipeng was Lin's eldest son.
units.literal: Jipeng was Lin's eldest son.

units.zh: 既立，更名昶，改元通文，以李仿判六軍諸衛事。
units.en: On taking the throne he changed his personal name to Chang, adopted the era name Pervading Culture, and appointed Li Fang commander of the Six Armies and palace guards.
units.literal: Once established he changed his name to Chang, altered the era name to Pervading Culture, and made Li Fang overseer of the Six Armies and all guards.

units.zh: 仿有弒君之罪，既立昶，而心常自疑，多養死士以為備。
units.en: Fang had murdered his sovereign. Even after Chang's enthronement he lived in constant fear and maintained a large corps of devoted fighters as insurance.
units.literal: Fang bore the crime of regicide; though Chang was now enthroned, he constantly doubted himself in his heart and kept many death-defying warriors as a precaution.

units.zh: 昶患之，因大享軍，伏甲擒仿殺之，梟其首於市。
units.en: Chang feared Fang's power. At a grand military feast he concealed armed men, seized Fang, and executed him, then displayed his head in the marketplace.
units.literal: Chang resented this; he therefore held a great feast for the army, hid armored men, seized Fang and killed him, and displayed his head in the marketplace.

units.zh: 仿部曲千人叛，燒啟聖門，奪仿首，奔於錢塘。
units.en: A thousand of Fang's personal troops mutinied, burned the Gate of Enlightened Sagacity, recovered their commander's head, and fled to Qiantang.
units.literal: A thousand of Fang's personal troops rebelled, burned the Gate of Enlightened Sagacity, seized Fang's head, and fled to Qiantang.

units.zh: 晉天福二年，昶遣使朝貢京師，高祖遣散騎常侍盧損冊昶閩王，拜其子繼恭臨海郡王。
units.en: In the second year of Tianfu, Chang sent tribute envoys to the Jin capital. Emperor Gaozu dispatched Lu Sun, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, to invest Chang as King of Min and appoint his son Jigong Prince of Linhai.
units.literal: In the second year of Tianfu of Jin, Chang sent envoys to the capital to present tribute; the founding emperor dispatched the Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Lu Sun to invest Chang as King of Min and appoint his son Jigong Prince of Linhai.

units.zh: 損至閩，昶稱疾不見，令繼恭主之。
units.en: When Sun arrived in Min, Chang pleaded illness and refused an audience, leaving Jigong to receive him.
units.literal: When Sun reached Min, Chang claimed illness and would not see him, ordering Jigong to receive him in his stead.

units.zh: 又遣中書舍人劉乙勞損於館，乙衣冠偉然，騶僮甚盛。
units.en: He also sent Secretariat Drafter Liu Yi to entertain Sun at the guesthouse. Yi appeared in magnificent dress with an imposing retinue of grooms and servants.
units.literal: He also sent the Secretariat Drafter Liu Yi to entertain Sun at the guesthouse; Yi was imposing in cap and robes, with a very grand escort of grooms and attendants.

units.zh: 他日損遇乙於途，布衣芒屩而已，損使人誚之曰：「鳳閣舍人，何偪下之甚也！」
units.en: Another day Sun met Yi on the road dressed in plain cloth and straw sandals. Sun sent a man to taunt him: "Phoenix Pavilion drafter, how far you have lowered yourself!"
units.literal: Another day Sun met Yi on the road wearing only plain cloth and straw sandals; Sun sent someone to mock him, saying: "Phoenix Pavilion drafter—how extremely you demean yourself!"

units.zh: 乙羞愧，以手掩面而走。
units.en: Mortified, Yi covered his face and fled.
units.literal: Yi was ashamed and, covering his face with his hands, fled.

units.zh: 昶聞之，怒損侵辱之，損還，昶無所答。
units.en: Chang was furious that Sun had humiliated his envoy. Sun returned home, and Chang offered no response to the court.
units.literal: When Chang heard of this he was angry that Sun had insulted them; Sun returned, and Chang made no reply.

units.zh: 而其子繼恭遣其佐鄭元弼隨損至京師貢方物，致書晉大臣，述昶意求以敵國禮相往來。
units.en: Meanwhile his son Jigong sent aide Zheng Yuanbi to accompany Sun to the capital with tribute goods and a letter to Jin ministers asking that Min and Jin exchange embassies as equal states.
units.literal: Yet his son Jigong sent his aide Zheng Yuanbi to follow Sun to the capital with local products as tribute, writing to Jin ministers to convey Chang's wish to treat each other with the ceremonies due between equal states.

units.zh: 高祖怒其不遜，下詔暴其罪，歸其貢物不納。
units.en: Gaozu was enraged by this insolence. He issued an edict listing their offenses and returned their tribute unaccepted.
units.literal: The founding emperor was angry at their insolence, issued an edict exposing their crimes, and returned their tribute goods without accepting them.

units.zh: 兵部員外郎李知損上書請籍沒其物而禁錮使者，於是以元弼下獄。
units.en: Li Zhisun, Vice Director of the Ministry of War, memorialized asking that the goods be confiscated and the envoys imprisoned. Yuanbi was thrown into jail.
units.literal: The Vice Director of the Ministry of War Li Zhisun memorialized requesting confiscation of their goods and imprisonment of the envoys; Yuanbi was therefore thrown into prison.

units.zh: 獄具引見，元弼俯伏曰：「昶，夷貊之君，不知禮義，陛下方示大信，以來遠人，臣將命無狀，願伏斧鑕，以贖昶罪。」
units.en: When the case was concluded Yuanbi was brought before the throne. He prostrated himself and said, "Chang is a barbarian ruler who knows nothing of propriety. Your Majesty is showing great faith to draw distant peoples to your court. I have failed in my mission and beg to accept the axe in Chang's stead."
units.literal: When the case was complete he was brought before the throne; Yuanbi prostrated himself and said: "Chang is a barbarian lord who knows nothing of ritual and righteousness; Your Majesty is just now displaying great faith to draw distant peoples; I discharged my commission disgracefully and wish to submit to the axe to atone for Chang's offense."

units.zh: 高祖乃赦元弼，遣歸。
units.en: Gaozu pardoned Yuanbi and sent him home.
units.literal: The founding emperor then pardoned Yuanbi and sent him home.

units.zh: 昶亦好巫，拜道士譚紫霄為正一先生，又拜陳守元為天師，而妖人林興以巫見幸，事無大小，興輒以寶皇語命之而後行。
units.en: Chang also dabbled in sorcery, naming the Daoist Tan Zixiao Lord of Orthodox Unity and Chen Shouyuan Celestial Master. The sorcerer Lin Xing won his favor, and no matter great or small was undertaken until Xing pronounced the Precious Emperor's command.
units.literal: Chang also favored sorcery, invested the Daoist Tan Zixiao as Lord of the Orthodox Unity, and again invested Chen Shouyuan as Celestial Master; the sorcerer Lin Xing won favor through witchcraft—matters great and small, Xing would issue commands in the Precious Emperor's words before they were carried out.

units.zh: 守元教昶起三清臺三層，以黃金數千斤鑄寶皇及元始天尊、太上老君像，日焚龍腦、薰陸諸香數斤，作樂於臺下，晝夜聲不輟，雲如此可求大還丹。
units.en: Shouyuan persuaded Chang to erect a three-tiered Terrace of the Three Pure Ones and cast statues of the Precious Emperor, the Primordial Heavenly Worthy, and the Supreme Lord Lao from thousands of jin of gold. Each day several jin of dragon-brain, spikenard, and other incense were burned while music played below the terrace without cease, day and night, on the promise that the Great Reverted Elixir could be obtained this way.
units.literal: Shouyuan taught Chang to build a three-tiered Three Pure Ones Terrace, cast images of the Precious Emperor, the Primordial Heavenly Worthy, and the Supreme Lord Lao with several thousand jin of gold, burn several jin daily of dragon-brain, spikenard, and other incense, and make music below the terrace day and night without cease, saying that thus one could obtain the Great Reverted Elixir.

units.zh: 三年夏，虹見其宮中，林興傳神言：「此宗室將為亂之兆也。」
units.en: In the summer of the third year a rainbow appeared in the palace. Lin Xing relayed a spirit message: "This is an omen that the imperial clan will rebel."
units.literal: In the summer of the third year a rainbow appeared in his palace; Lin Xing relayed a spirit message: "This is an omen that the imperial clan will bring rebellion."

units.zh: 乃命興率壯士殺審知子延武、延望及其子五人。
units.en: He ordered Xing to lead bravos to kill Shenzhi's sons Yanwu and Yanwang along with five of their sons.
units.literal: He then ordered Xing to lead stalwart men to kill Shenzhi's sons Yanwu and Yanwang and their five sons.

units.zh: 後興事敗，亦被殺。
units.en: When Xing's plot collapsed he too was executed.
units.literal: Later Xing's affair failed and he too was killed.

units.zh: 而昶愈惑亂，立父婢春燕為淑妃，後立以為皇后。
units.en: Chang grew only more erratic. He made his father's maid Spring Swallow a Pure Consort and later elevated her to empress.
units.literal: Yet Chang grew ever more confused and disorderly; he installed his father's maid Spring Swallow as Pure Consort and later raised her to empress.

units.zh: 又遣醫人陳究以空名堂牒賣官。
units.en: He also had the physician Chen Jiu sell offices using blank appointment documents.
units.literal: He also sent the physician Chen Jiu to sell offices with blank Hall memorials.

units.zh: 昶弟繼嚴判六軍諸衛事，昶疑而罷之，代以季弟繼鏞，而募勇士為宸衛都以自衛，其賜予給賞，獨厚於他軍。
units.en: Chang's brother Jiyan commanded the Six Armies and palace guards. Chang suspected him, removed him, and replaced him with his youngest brother Jiyong. He then recruited stalwart men into an Imperial Guard Command for his personal protection and lavished on them rewards richer than those given any other unit.
units.literal: Chang's brother Jiyan oversaw the Six Armies and all guards; Chang suspected him and dismissed him, replacing him with his youngest brother Jiyong; he recruited stalwart men for the Imperial Guard Command to protect himself, whose grants and rewards alone were richer than the other armies.

units.zh: 控鶴都將連重遇、拱宸都將朱文進，皆以此怒激其軍。
units.en: The Crane-Control commander Lian Chongyu and the Arch-Palace commander Zhu Wenjin incited their troops to fury over this favoritism.
units.literal: The Crane-Control Commanders Lian Chongyu and the Arch-Palace Commanders Zhu Wenjin both roused their troops to anger over this.

units.zh: 是歲夏，術者言昶宮中當有災，昶徙南宮避災，而宮中火，昶疑重遇軍士縱火。
units.en: That summer diviners warned of disaster in the palace. Chang moved to the Southern Palace to escape it, but fire broke out anyway. Chang suspected soldiers under Chongyu of arson.
units.literal: That summer diviners said disaster would strike within Chang's palace; Chang moved to the Southern Palace to avoid calamity, but fire broke out in the palace; Chang suspected soldiers of Chongyu's command had set the blaze.

units.zh: 內學士陳郯素以便佞為昶所親信，昶以火事語之，郯反以告重遇。
units.en: The Inner Academician Chen Tan had long won Chang's trust through flattery. Chang confided his suspicions about the fire to Tan, who promptly warned Chongyu.
units.literal: The Inner Academician Chen Tan had long won Chang's trust through flattery; Chang spoke to him about the fire, and Tan in turn informed Chongyu.

units.zh: 重遇懼，夜率衛士縱火焚南宮，昶挾愛姬、子弟、黃門衛士斬關而出，宿於野次。
units.en: Terrified, Chongyu led his guards that night to burn the Southern Palace. Chang fled with his favorite consorts, sons, and eunuch guards, cutting his way through the gates to camp in the open countryside.
units.literal: Chongyu was afraid; that night he led guards to set fire and burn the Southern Palace; Chang took his favorite consorts, sons, and eunuch guards, cut through the gates and fled, lodging in the open countryside.

units.zh: 重遇迎延義立之。
units.en: Chongyu welcomed Yanyi and set him on the throne.
units.literal: Chongyu welcomed Yanyi and installed him.

units.zh: 延義令其子繼業率兵襲昶，及之；
units.en: Yanyi sent his son Jiye with troops to pursue Chang and overtook him.
units.literal: Yanyi ordered his son Jiye to lead troops in pursuit of Chang and overtook him;

units.zh: 射殺數人，昶知不免，擲弓於地，繼業執而殺之，及其妻、子皆死無遺類。
units.en: Several of Chang's party were shot down. Seeing escape was impossible, Chang threw down his bow. Jiye seized him and killed him, and his wife and sons were slaughtered to the last person.
units.literal: several were shot dead; Chang knew he could not escape, cast his bow to the ground; Jiye seized and killed him, and his wife and sons all died without a survivor.

units.zh: 延義立，謚昶曰康宗。
units.en: With Yanyi enthroned, Chang was posthumously titled Sovereign Kang.
units.literal: Yanyi took the throne and gave Chang the posthumous title Sovereign Kang.

units.zh: 延義，審知少子也。
units.en: Yanyi was Shenzhi's youngest son.
units.literal: Yanyi was Shenzhi's youngest son.

units.zh: 既立，更名曦，遣使者朝貢於晉，改元永隆。
units.en: On taking power he changed his personal name to Xi, sent tribute envoys to Jin, and adopted the era name Eternal Ascent.
units.literal: Once established he changed his name to Xi, sent envoys to present tribute to Jin, and altered the era name to Eternal Ascent.

units.zh: 鑄大鐵錢，以一當十。
units.en: He cast large iron coins, each reckoned as ten ordinary coins.
units.literal: He cast large iron coins valued at ten to one.

units.zh: 曦自昶世倔強難制，昶相王倓每抑折之，曦亦憚倓，不敢有所發。
units.en: Xi had been unruly and defiant even under Chang. Chang's chancellor Wang Tan had repeatedly reined him in, and Xi feared Tan enough to keep his resentment hidden.
units.literal: Xi had been stubborn and hard to control since Chang's reign; Chang's chancellor Wang Tan often repressed and checked him, and Xi also feared Tan and dared not act out.

units.zh: 新羅遣使聘閩以寶劍，昶舉以示倓曰：「此將何為？」
units.en: Silla sent envoys to Min bearing a precious sword. Chang held it up for Tan and asked, "What do you suppose this is for?"
units.literal: Silla sent envoys to Min with a precious sword as a gift; Chang held it up to show Tan and said: "What is this for?"

units.zh: 倓曰：「不忠不孝者，斬之。」
units.en: Tan replied, "To behead the disloyal and unfilial."
units.literal: Tan said: "To behead the disloyal and unfilial."

units.zh: 曦居旁色變。
units.en: Xi, standing nearby, turned pale.
units.literal: Xi, standing nearby, changed color.

units.zh: 曦既立，而新羅復獻劍，曦思倓前言，而倓已死，命發冢戮其屍，倓面如生，血流被體。
units.en: After Xi took the throne Silla sent another sword. Remembering Tan's earlier remark, and learning Tan was dead, Xi ordered his tomb opened and his corpse flogged. Tan's face looked as if he were alive, and blood streamed over his body.
units.literal: Once Xi was enthroned Silla again presented a sword; Xi recalled Tan's earlier words, but Tan was already dead; he ordered the tomb opened and the corpse flogged; Tan's face was as if alive and blood flowed over his body.

units.zh: 泉州刺史余廷英嘗矯曦命掠取良家子，曦怒，召下御史劾之。
units.en: Quanzhou prefect Yu Tingying had forged Xi's orders to seize daughters of respectable families. Xi was furious and ordered the censors to prosecute him.
units.literal: The Quanzhou prefect Yu Tingying had once forged Xi's orders to seize daughters of good families; Xi was angry and summoned the censors to prosecute him.

units.zh: 廷英進買宴錢千萬，曦曰：「皇后土貢何在？」
units.en: Tingying offered ten million cash to buy his way out of prosecution. Xi demanded, "Where is the empress's tribute?"
units.literal: Tingying presented ten million in banquet-purchase money; Xi said: "Where is the empress's local tribute?"

units.zh: 廷英又獻皇后錢千萬，乃得不劾。
units.en: Tingying paid another ten million for the empress and was spared prosecution.
units.literal: Tingying again presented ten million for the empress, and only then escaped prosecution.

units.zh: 曦嘗嫁女，朝士有不賀者笞之。
units.en: When Xi married off a daughter, any court official who failed to offer congratulations was flogged.
units.literal: When Xi married off a daughter, court officials who did not offer congratulations were flogged.

units.zh: 御史中丞劉贊坐不糾舉，將加笞，諫議大夫鄭元弼切諫，曦謂元弼曰：「卿何如魏鄭公，乃敢強諫！」
units.en: Censor-in-Chief Liu Zan was charged with failing to impeach the offenders and was about to be flogged. Remonstrance Counselor Zheng Yuanbi protested sharply. Xi told him, "What makes you think you are Duke Wei of Zheng that you dare remonstrate so boldly?"
units.literal: The Censor-in-Chief Liu Zan was charged with failing to impeach and was about to be flogged; the Remonstrance Counselor Zheng Yuanbi remonstrated forcefully; Xi said to Yuanbi: "In what way are you like Duke Wei of Zheng that you dare remonstrate so strongly!"

units.zh: 元弼曰：「陛下似唐太宗，臣為魏鄭公可矣。」
units.en: Yuanbi replied, "If Your Majesty resembles Emperor Taizong of Tang, then I may well play the part of Duke Wei of Zheng."
units.literal: Yuanbi said: "Your Majesty resembles Emperor Taizong of Tang; I may well serve as Duke Wei of Zheng."

units.zh: 曦喜，乃釋贊不笞。
units.en: Xi was amused and spared Zan the flogging.
units.literal: Xi was pleased and released Zan without flogging.

units.zh: 曦弟延政為建州節度使，封富沙王，自曦立，不葉，數舉兵相攻，曦由此惡其宗室，多以事誅之。
units.en: Xi's brother Yanzheng, military governor of Jianzhou and Prince of Fusha, had been at odds with him since Xi's enthronement and repeatedly marched against him. Xi came to hate his own clan and executed many kinsmen on one pretext or another.
units.literal: Xi's brother Yanzheng was military governor of Jian Prefecture, enfeoffed as Prince of Fusha; since Xi's enthronement they were not on good terms and repeatedly raised troops against each other; Xi therefore hated his clan and killed many of them on various charges.

units.zh: 諫議大夫黃峻舁櫬詣朝堂極諫，曦怒，貶峻漳州司戶參軍。
units.en: Remonstrance Counselor Huang Jun carried his own coffin into court and remonstrated to the limit. Xi was enraged and demoted him to registrar in Zhangzhou.
units.literal: The Remonstrance Counselor Huang Jun carried his coffin to the court hall and remonstrated to the utmost; Xi was angry and demoted Jun to Registrar of Zhang Prefecture.

units.zh: 校書郎陳光逸上書疏曦過惡五十餘事，曦命衛士鞭之百而不死，以繩系頸，掛於木，久而乃絕。
units.en: Proofreader Chen Guangyi submitted a memorial listing more than fifty of Xi's crimes. Xi ordered guards to flog him a hundred strokes without killing him, then bound a rope around his neck and hung him from a tree until he finally died.
units.literal: The Proofreader Chen Guangyi submitted a memorial listing more than fifty of Xi's faults and crimes; Xi ordered guards to flog him a hundred strokes without killing him, tied a rope around his neck, hung him from a tree, and only after a long while did he die.

units.zh: 國計使陳匡范增算商之法以獻，曦曰：「匡範人中寶也。」
units.en: National Revenue Commissioner Chen Kuangfan proposed heavier merchant taxes. Xi declared, "Kuangfan is a treasure among men."
units.literal: The National Revenue Commissioner Chen Kuangfan presented a plan to increase merchant tax assessments; Xi said: "Kuangfan is a treasure among men."

units.zh: 已而歲入不登其數，乃借於民以足之，匡範以憂死。
units.en: When annual revenue still fell short, officials borrowed from the people to make up the deficit. Kuangfan died of anxiety.
units.literal: Before long the year's revenue did not reach the target figure, so they borrowed from the people to make it up; Kuangfan died of anxiety.

units.zh: 其後知其借於民也，剖棺斷屍，棄之水中。
units.en: When Xi later learned the deficit had been covered by forced loans from the people, he had Kuangfan's coffin opened, the corpse dismembered, and the remains thrown into the river.
units.literal: Later, learning that the shortfall had been made up by borrowing from the people, he opened the coffin, dismembered the corpse, and cast it into the water.

units.zh: 曦性既淫虐，而妻李氏悍而酗酒，賢妃尚氏有色而寵。
units.en: Xi was by nature lewd and cruel. His wife Lady Li was fierce and a heavy drinker, while the Worthy Consort Lady Shang was beautiful and held his favor.
units.literal: Xi's nature was already lewd and cruel; his wife the Lady Li was fierce and given to heavy drinking; the Worthy Consort the Lady Shang was beautiful and favored.

units.zh: 李仁遇，曦甥也，以色嬖之，用以為相。
units.en: Li Renyu, Xi's nephew, won favor through his beauty and was made chancellor.
units.literal: Li Renyu was Xi's nephew by his sister; Xi favored him for his looks and made him chancellor.

units.zh: 曦常為牛飲，群臣侍酒，醉而不勝，有訴及私棄酒者輒殺之。
units.en: Xi often held drinking contests in which ministers had to keep pace. Anyone who became too drunk to continue, or was reported to have secretly discarded wine, was executed on the spot.
units.literal: Xi often held ox drinking-bouts; the ministers attended with wine; those who became drunk beyond endurance, or were reported to have secretly poured away wine, were immediately killed.

units.zh: 諸子繼柔棄酒，並殺其贊者一人。
units.en: When his son Jirou poured away wine, Xi also executed one of the attendants who had urged him to drink.
units.literal: When his son Jirou poured away wine, he also killed one of the attendants who urged him on.

units.zh: 連重遇殺昶，懼為國人所討，與朱文進連姻以自固。
units.en: Lian Chongyu, who had killed Chang, feared popular retribution and cemented his position by marrying into Zhu Wenjin's family.
units.literal: Lian Chongyu had killed Chang and feared the people of the state would rise against him; he allied his family by marriage with Zhu Wenjin to strengthen himself.

units.zh: 曦心疑之，常以語誚重遇等，重遇等流涕自辨。
units.en: Xi grew suspicious of them and often taunted Chongyu and his allies, who wept as they protested their loyalty.
units.literal: Xi harbored suspicion in his heart and often mocked Chongyu and the others in speech; Chongyu and the others wept as they defended themselves.

units.zh: 李氏妒尚妃之寵，欲圖曦而立其子亞澄，乃使人謂重遇等曰：「上心不平於二公，奈何？」
units.en: Lady Li, jealous of Worthy Consort Shang, plotted to overthrow Xi and install her son Yacheng. She sent word to Chongyu and his allies: "The emperor's heart has turned against you—what will you do?"
units.literal: The Lady Li was jealous of Worthy Consort Shang's favor, wished to plot against Xi and install her son Yacheng, and therefore sent someone to tell Chongyu and the others: "The emperor's heart is ill-disposed toward you two—what is to be done?"

units.zh: 重遇等懼。
units.en: Chongyu and his men were terrified.
units.literal: Chongyu and the others were afraid.

units.zh: 六年三月，曦出遊，醉歸，重遇等遣壯士拉於馬上而殺之，謚曰景宗。
units.en: In the third month of the sixth year Xi went out on an excursion and returned drunk. Chongyu and his allies sent bravos to pull him onto a horse and kill him. He was posthumously titled Sovereign Jing.
units.literal: In the third month of the sixth year Xi went out on an excursion and returned drunk; Chongyu and the others sent stalwart men to drag him onto a horse and kill him; his posthumous title was Sovereign Jing.

units.zh: 延政，審知子也。
units.en: Yanzheng was a son of Shenzhi.
units.literal: Yanzheng was Shenzhi's son.

units.zh: 曦立，為淫虐，延政數貽書諫之。
units.en: After Xi took the throne and ruled with cruelty and debauchery, Yanzheng repeatedly sent letters of remonstrance.
units.literal: When Xi was enthroned and became lewd and cruel, Yanzheng repeatedly sent letters remonstrating with him.

units.zh: 曦怒，遣杜建崇監其軍，延政逐之，曦乃舉兵攻延政，為延政所敗。
units.en: Xi was furious and sent Du Jianchong to supervise Yanzheng's army. Yanzheng expelled him, and when Xi marched against him he was defeated.
units.literal: Xi was angry and sent Du Jianchong to supervise his army; Yanzheng drove him out; Xi then raised troops to attack Yanzheng and was defeated by him.

units.zh: 延政乃以建州建國稱殷，改元天德。
units.en: Yanzheng then founded the state of Yin at Jianzhou and adopted the era name Heavenly Virtue.
units.literal: Yanzheng then founded a state at Jian Prefecture, declared himself ruler of Yin, and changed the era name to Heavenly Virtue.

units.zh: 明年，連重遇已殺曦，集閩羣臣告曰：「昔太袓武皇帝親冒矢石，遂啟有閩，及其子孫，淫虐不道。
units.en: The following year, after Lian Chongyu had killed Xi, he gathered the ministers of Min and declared: "Long ago the founding Martial Emperor braved arrows and stones and opened rule in Min. Yet his descendants have been lewd, cruel, and without the Way.
units.literal: The next year, Lian Chongyu having already killed Xi, gathered the ministers of Min and announced: "In former days the founding Martial Emperor personally braved arrows and stones and thereby opened rule in Min. Yet his descendants have been lewd, cruel, and without the Way.

units.zh: 今天厭王氏，百姓與能，當求有德，以安此土。」
units.en: Heaven now rejects the Wang clan, and the people seek a worthy ruler. We must find a man of virtue to settle this land."
units.literal: Heaven now rejects the Wang clan; the people seek a worthy man. We must find one of virtue to settle this land."

units.zh: 羣臣皆莫敢議，乃掖朱文進升殿，率百官北面而臣之。
units.en: No minister dared object. They helped Zhu Wenjin onto the throne and led the officials to bow north and acknowledge him as sovereign.
units.literal: None of the ministers dared speak; they then helped Zhu Wenjin up to the hall and led all officials to face north and serve him as sovereign.

units.zh: 文進以重遇判六軍諸衞事，王氏子弟在福州者無少長皆殺之。
units.en: Wenjin put Chongyu in charge of the Six Armies and palace guards. Every Wang clansman in Fuzhou, young or old, was killed.
units.literal: Wenjin put Chongyu in charge of the Six Armies and all guards. Every Wang clansman in Fuzhou, young or old, was killed.

units.zh: 以黃紹頗守泉州，程贇守漳州，許文縝守汀州，稱晉年號，時開運元年也。
units.en: He appointed Huang Shaopo to hold Quanzhou, Cheng Yun to hold Zhangzhou, and Xu Wenzhen to hold Tingzhou, and adopted Jin era names. It was the first year of Kaiyun.
units.literal: He appointed Huang Shaopo to hold Quanzhou, Cheng Yun to hold Zhangzhou, and Xu Wenzhen to hold Tingzhou, and adopted Jin era names—it was then the first year of Kaiyun.

units.zh: 泉州軍將留從効詐其州人曰：「富沙王兵收福州矣，吾屬世為王氏臣，安能交臂而事賊乎？」
units.en: The Quanzhou officer Liu Congxiao deceived the people of the prefecture, saying, "The Prince of Fusha's troops have already taken Fuzhou. We have been Wang subjects for generations—how can we fold our arms and serve rebels?"
units.literal: The Quanzhou officer Liu Congxiao deceived the people of the prefecture, saying: "The Prince of Fusha's troops have already taken Fuzhou. We have been Wang subjects for generations—how can we fold our arms and serve bandits?"

units.zh: 州人共殺紹頗，迎王繼勳為刺史，漳州聞之，亦殺贇，迎王繼成為刺史，皆王氏之諸子也。
units.en: The people of Quanzhou killed Shaopo and welcomed Wang Jixun as prefect. Zhangzhou heard of this, killed Yun, and welcomed Wang Jicheng as prefect. Both were sons of the Wang clan.
units.literal: The people of the prefecture jointly killed Shaopo and welcomed Wang Jixun as prefect. Hearing this, Zhangzhou also killed Yun and welcomed Wang Jicheng as prefect—both were sons of the Wang clan.

units.zh: 文縝懼，以汀州降于延政。
units.en: Wenzhen, in fear, surrendered Tingzhou to Yanzheng.
units.literal: Wenzhen was afraid and surrendered Tingzhou to Yanzheng.

units.zh: 延政已得三州，重遇亦殺文進，傳首建州以自歸。
units.en: Yanzheng had already gained three prefectures. Chongyu also killed Wenjin and sent his head to Jianzhou in submission.
units.literal: Yanzheng had already gained three prefectures. Chongyu also killed Wenjin and sent his head to Jianzhou to submit himself.

units.zh: 福州裨將林仁翰又殺重遇，謀迎延政都福州。
units.en: The Fuzhou adjutant Lin Renhan then killed Chongyu and plotted to bring Yanzheng to Fuzhou as ruler.
units.literal: The Fuzhou adjutant Lin Renhan then killed Chongyu and plotted to welcome Yanzheng to rule Fuzhou.

units.zh: 是時，南唐李景聞閩亂，發兵攻之，延政遣其從子繼昌守福州，而南唐兵方急攻延政，福州將李仁達謂其徒曰：「唐兵攻建州，富沙王不能自保，其能有此土也？」
units.en: Li Jing of Southern Tang, hearing of chaos in Min, sent an army to attack. Yanzheng sent his nephew Jichang to hold Fuzhou. While Tang forces pressed Yanzheng hard, Fuzhou general Li Renda told his men, "Tang troops are attacking Jianzhou. The Prince of Fusha cannot even save himself—how can he hold this land?"
units.literal: At that time Li Jing of Southern Tang, hearing of turmoil in Min, sent troops to attack; Yanzheng dispatched his nephew Jichang to hold Fuzhou; while Southern Tang forces were pressing hard against Yanzheng, the Fuzhou general Li Renda said to his followers: "Tang troops are attacking Jian Prefecture; the Prince of Fusha cannot even protect himself—how could he hold this territory?"

units.zh: 乃擒繼昌殺之。
units.en: He seized Jichang and killed him.
units.literal: He then seized Jichang and killed him.

units.zh: 欲自立，懼眾不附，以雪峰寺僧卓儼明示眾曰：「此非常人也。」
units.en: Wishing to rule himself but fearing the troops would not follow him, he presented the monk Zhuo Yanming of Xuefeng Temple to the crowd, declaring, "This is no ordinary man."
units.literal: Wishing to rule himself but fearing the multitude would not follow, he had the Xuefeng Temple monk Zhuo Yanming show himself to the crowd, saying: "This is no ordinary man."

units.zh: 被以袞冕，率諸將吏北面而臣之。
units.en: They dressed him in imperial robes and led the generals and officials to bow to him as their sovereign.
units.literal: They clothed him in imperial robes and caps, and the generals and officials led them all to face north and serve him as sovereign.

units.zh: 已而又殺儼明，乃自立，送款於李景，景以仁達為威武軍節度使，更其名曰弘義。
units.en: Soon he killed Yanming as well and ruled in his own name. He submitted to Li Jing, who appointed him military governor of the Weiwu Army and changed his name to Hongyi.
units.literal: Before long he killed Yanming as well and ruled himself; he sent submission to Li Jing; Jing appointed Renda military governor of the Weiwu Army and changed his name to Hongyi.

units.zh: 而景兵攻破建州，遷延政族於金陵，封鄱陽王。
units.en: Tang forces then captured Jianzhou, moved Yanzheng's clan to Jinling, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Poyang.
units.literal: Jing's troops then captured Jian Prefecture, moved Yanzheng's clan to Jinling, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Poyang.

units.zh: 是歲，景保大四年也。
units.en: This occurred in the fourth year of Jing's Baoda era.
units.literal: That year was the fourth year of Baoda of Jing.

units.zh: 留從效聞延政降唐，執王繼勛送於金陵，李景以泉州為清源軍，以從效為節度使。
units.en: When Liu Congxiao learned Yanzheng had surrendered to Tang, he seized Wang Jixun and sent him to Jinling. Li Jing organized Quanzhou as the Qingyuan military circuit and appointed Congxiao its governor.
units.literal: Liu Congxiao, hearing that Yanzheng had submitted to Tang, seized Wang Jixun and sent him to Jinling; Li Jing made Quanzhou the Qingyuan Army district and appointed Congxiao its military governor.

units.zh: 景已破延政，遣人召李仁達入朝，仁達不從，遂降於吳越。
units.en: After defeating Yanzheng, Jing summoned Li Renda to court. Renda refused and submitted to Wuyue instead.
units.literal: Jing had already defeated Yanzheng and sent someone to summon Li Renda to court; Renda would not obey and therefore submitted to Wuyue.

units.zh: 而留從效亦逐景守兵，據泉、漳二州，景猶封從效晉江王。
units.en: Liu Congxiao also expelled Tang garrisons and held Quanzhou and Zhangzhou. Jing still enfeoffed him as Prince of Jinjiang.
units.literal: Liu Congxiao also drove out Jing's garrison troops and held the two prefectures of Quan and Zhang; Jing still enfeoffed Congxiao as Prince of Jinjiang.

units.zh: 周世宗時，從效遣牙將蔡仲興為商人，間道至京師，求置邸內屬。
units.en: During the reign of Emperor Shizong of Zhou, Congxiao sent general Cai Zhongxing disguised as a merchant along a secret route to the capital to request a diplomatic lodge and recognition as a Zhou dependency.
units.literal: During the reign of Emperor Shizong of Zhou, Congxiao sent general Cai Zhongxing disguised as a merchant along a secret route to the capital to request a diplomatic lodge and recognition as a Zhou dependency.

units.zh: 是時，世宗與李景畫江為界，遂不納，從效仍臣於南唐。
units.en: Shizong had just drawn the Yangtze as his boundary with Li Jing and declined the request. Congxiao remained a vassal of Southern Tang.
units.literal: At that time Shizong and Li Jing had drawn the Yangtze as a boundary, so he did not accept them; Congxiao still submitted to Southern Tang.

units.zh: 其後事具國史。
units.en: Later events are recorded in full in the dynastic histories.
units.literal: Subsequent events are fully recorded in the dynastic histories.

units.zh: 晉開運三年丙午，南唐保大四年也。
units.en: The third year of Kaiyun of Jin, the bingwu year, was the fourth year of Baoda of Southern Tang.
units.literal: In the third year of Kaiyun of Jin, bingwu—the fourth year of Baoda of Southern Tang.

units.zh: 是歲，李景兵破建州，王氏滅。
units.en: That year Li Jing's army captured Jianzhou and the Wang clan was destroyed.
units.literal: That year Li Jing's troops captured Jianzhou and the Wang clan was destroyed.

units.zh: 江南錄云：「保大三年，虜王氏之族，遷于金陵。」
units.en: The Jiangnan Record says, "In the third year of Baoda the Wang clan was taken captive and moved to Jinling."
units.literal: The Jiangnan Record says: "In the third year of Baoda the Wang clan was taken captive and moved to Jinling."

units.zh: 謬也。
units.en: This is wrong.
units.literal: This is mistaken.

units.zh: 據王潮實以唐景福元年入福州，拜觀察使，而後人紀錄者，乃用「騎馬來、騎馬去」之讖以為據，遂以王潮光啟二年歲在丙午拜泉州刺史為始年，至保大四年，歲復在丙午而滅，故為六十一年。
units.en: Wang Chao actually entered Fuzhou in the first year of Jingfu of Tang and was appointed observation commissioner. Later chroniclers, guided by the prophecy "came on horseback, left on horseback," took Wang Chao's appointment as Quanzhou prefect in the second year of Guangqi, a bingwu year, as the founding date. The state fell in the fourth year of Baoda, when bingwu came round again—hence sixty-one years.
units.literal: In fact Wang Chao entered Fuzhou in the first year of Jingfu of Tang and was appointed observation commissioner. Later chroniclers, relying on the prophecy "came on horseback, left on horseback," took Wang Chao's appointment as Quanzhou prefect in the second year of Guangqi, a bingwu year, as the founding date. The state was destroyed in the fourth year of Baoda, when bingwu came round again—hence sixty-one years.

units.zh: 然其奄有閩國，則當自景福元年為始，實五十五年也。
units.en: But from the time they fully held the Min realm, the count should begin with the first year of Jingfu—fifty-five years in all.
units.literal: But from the time the Wangs fully held the Min realm, the count should begin with the first year of Jingfu—fifty-five years in fact.

units.zh: 今諸家記其國滅丙午是也。
units.en: Present accounts correctly record the state's destruction in a bingwu year.
units.literal: Current accounts correctly record the state's destruction in a bingwu year.

units.zh: 其始年則牽於讖書，繆矣。
units.en: The founding date is wrong because it was dictated by a prophecy text.
units.literal: The error lies in the founding date, which was dictated by a prophecy text.

units.zh: 惟江南錄又差其末年也。
units.en: Only the Jiangnan Record is also one year off at the end.
units.literal: Only the Jiangnan Record is also off by one year at the end.
